value.text: Quality-relevant time series data from the Digital Factory machines (IMM, Laser Engraver, Delta Robot). Data is exchanged in JSON format. Live values are published over MQTT (Mosquitto broker); historical records are stored in TimescaleDB and exposed over a FastAPI REST API. Only quality-related measurements are exposed in this submodel — defect counts, good-part counts, cycle times and completion progress — filtered from each machine's full data stream. Each record holds one measurement: Time, MachineId, MetricName, Value, Unit.
Quality metrics from the IMM: good_parts, bad_parts, parts_remaining, avg_cycle_time_ms, last_cycle_time_ms.
Quality metrics from the Laser Engraver: count_finished_card, last_job_duration_s, total_engraving_duration_s, progress.
Quality metrics from the Delta Robot: successful_picks, failed_picks, cycle_time_ms.
Six static sample records - two quality measurements per machine, embedded as a Type 1 snapshot.

description.text: KPI values currently displayed on the dashboard panels. These are views derived from each machine's data (IMM, Laser Engraver, Delta Robot) and refreshed via MQTT and FastAPI REST. The authoritative data resides in each machine's own AAS; this submodel represents what the dashboard renders at a given moment.

Availability is the proportion of scheduled production time during which the machine was available for production. Calculated as actual_run_time / planned_production_time. One of the three OEE pillars (Availability × Performance × Quality = OEE).
Performance is the ratio of actual production speed to the ideal/maximum speed. Calculated as (ideal_cycle_time × total_count) / run_time. One of the three OEE pillars.
Quality is the proportion of good parts out of total parts produced. Calculated as good_count / total_count. One of the three OEE pillars and the direct quality indicator within OEE.

Overall Equipment Effectiveness is the composite manufacturing performance metric calculated as Availability × Performance × Quality. World-class OEE is typically considered 85% or above. Standard benchmark of manufacturing productivity.
